hypothesis.uncertainty: The team does not yet know whether the current persistence strategy can support the projected write volume without degrading the user experience.
hypothesis.title: Validate the storage write capacity
hypothesis.statement: The current persistence architecture supports the expected write peak without exceeding the agreed latency limit.
hypothesis.justification: This hypothesis can be checked with a controlled load test before committing the team to an architectural change. The result compares current capacity with projected demand and makes the point at which an alternative is needed explicit.

assessment.impact_justification: Persistence degradation affects essential operations and can block user workflows.
assessment.uncertainty_justification: Initial metrics are available, but they do not yet represent simultaneous write peaks.

technical_plan.rationale: Measure representative load behavior before deciding whether the architecture needs to change.

items.title: Run a controlled load experiment
items.objective: Compare latency and error rates against the product's agreed limits.
items.description: Reproduce the expected peak in an isolated environment, gradually increase concurrency, and record p95 latency, saturation, and write errors.
items.tradeoff: Requires representative data and environment setup, but avoids a premature migration.

items.title: Define a persistence reassessment trigger
items.objective: Make it clear when an architectural alternative should be evaluated.
items.description: Document the latency and error thresholds that trigger a new assessment, including who monitors the metrics after release.
items.tradeoff: Defers the structural decision and requires ongoing metric monitoring.
